## 1. Model from PWS Segment (DHS2024)
### 1.1. Get full variable list
```{r}
pws.tt.rural <- readRDS("../data/tree_rural_pruned.rds")
pws.tt.urban <- readRDS("../data/tree_urban_pruned.rds")
```

#### 1.1.1. Rural
```{r}
# Variables used in primary splits
rural_vars <- unique(pws.tt.rural$frame$var)
rural_vars <- rural_vars[rural_vars != "<leaf>"]
cat("Rural model variables:\n")
print(rural_vars)
```

#### 1.1.2. Urban
```{r}

urban_vars <- urban_vars[urban_vars != "<leaf>"]
cat("\nUrban model variables:\n")
print(urban_vars)
```


## 2. Train new trees
```{r}
cat("\nNN and Mindset variables were mapped to try and apply NNDHS2024 TT to Mindset data, but few variables overlapped. So we recreated a TT based on overlapping variables between the two datasets\n")
```

```{r}
# urban	LCA4_class
# rural	LCA5_class

# Use segment_rank insead of LCAk_class
urban$segment_rank <- as.factor(urban$segment_rank)
urban.kano$segment_rank <- as.factor(urban.kano$segment_rank)
rural$segment_rank <- as.factor(rural$segment_rank)
rural.kano$segment_rank <- as.factor(rural.kano$segment_rank)
```

### 2.1. Urban tree
#### 2.1.1. National
```{r}
tree_urban <- rpart(segment_rank ~ any.hh.dis + ed.sec.higher + has.mobile + hh.animal + hh.clean.fuel + hh.land + hh.noimp.housing + hh.noimp.wall + hh.rooms.cat + hh.toilet.flush + marr.cohab + med.alone + med.cost + med.dist + med.permis + muslim + occupation.cat1 + partner.working.yn + rad.yn + tv.yn + wealth.sum.index.cat1 + working.yn, data=urban, control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")

plotcp(tree_urban)
printcp(tree_urban)
```

```{r}
tree_urban_prune<-prune(tree_urban, cp=0.001)
```

```{r, fig.height=10, fig.width= 18}
# Look at sensitivity/specificity/etc for pruned tree
PredictCART_train_urban <- predict(tree_urban_prune, data=urban, type="class")
confusionMatrix(data=PredictCART_train_urban, as.factor(urban$segment_rank))

prp(tree_urban_prune, type=5, varlen=0, cex=1)
#fancyRpartPlot(tree_urban_prune, type = 3, cex = 0.7, caption = NULL, uniform=T)
```

#### 2.1.2. National with penalty
```{r}
#  Grow a tree with loss penalty for U2-NN
cls <- levels(urban$segment_rank)
K   <- length(cls)

loss <- matrix(1, nrow = K, ncol = K, dimnames = list(cls, cls))
diag(loss) <- 0
loss["U2-NN", ] <- 1.1   # stronger penalty for harder segment
loss["U2-NN", "U2-NN"] <- 0

tree_urban <- rpart(segment_rank ~ any.hh.dis + ed.sec.higher + has.mobile + hh.animal + hh.clean.fuel + hh.land + hh.noimp.housing + hh.noimp.wall + hh.rooms.cat + hh.toilet.flush + marr.cohab + med.alone + med.cost + med.dist + med.permis + muslim + occupation.cat1 + partner.working.yn + rad.yn + tv.yn + wealth.sum.index.cat1 + working.yn, data=urban, parms = list(loss = loss), control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")
plotcp(tree_urban)
printcp(tree_urban)
# See what is the cp value if following 1-SE rule 
cp_table <- as.data.frame(tree_urban$cptable)
# minimum xerror row
min_row <- which.min(cp_table$xerror)
# threshold = min xerror + its standard error
threshold <- cp_table$xerror[min_row] + cp_table$xstd[min_row]

# pick the LARGEST cp (= simplest tree) whose xerror is still within threshold
cp_1se <- cp_table$CP[max(which(cp_table$xerror <= threshold))]

cat("cp chosen by 1-SE rule:", cp_1se, "\n")
cat("cp chosen by min-xerror:", cp_table$CP[min_row], "\n")
#both suggesting 0.001; but then the tree is unnecessarily big, and the line starts flattened from0.02, so adjust it to 0.002)
tree_urban_prune <- prune(tree_urban, cp = 0.002)
```

```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=20}
prp(tree_urban_prune, type=5, varlen=0, cex=0.9, extra = 2)

pred <- predict(tree_urban_prune, urban, type = "class")
confusionMatrix(pred, urban$segment_rank)
```

#### 2.2.2. National with penalty (not better, sacrifice R2)
```{r}
#  Grow a tree with loss penalty for R3.1 and R4.1 
cls <- levels(rural$segment_rank)
K   <- length(cls)

loss <- matrix(1, nrow = K, ncol = K, dimnames = list(cls, cls))
diag(loss) <- 0
loss["R3.1-NN", ] <- 1.6   # stronger penalty for harder segment
loss["R3.1-NN", "R3.1-NN"] <- 0
loss["R4.1-NN",   ] <- 1.4
loss["R4.1-NN",   "R4.1-NN"]   <- 0

tree_rural <- rpart(segment_rank ~ any.hh.dis + ed.level + hh.mobile + hh.animal + hh.clean.fuel + hh.land + hh.noimp.housing + hh.noimp.wall + hh.rooms.cat + hh.toilet.flush + marr.cohab + med.alone + med.cost + med.dist + med.permis + muslim + religion + occupation.cat1 + partner.working.yn + rad.yn + tv.yn + wealth.sum.index.cat1 + working.yn, data=rural, parms = list(loss = loss), control=rpart.control(cp=0.001, xval=5), method="class")
plotcp(tree_rural)
printcp(tree_rural)
# See what is the cp value if following 1-SE rule 
cp_table <- as.data.frame(tree_rural$cptable)
# minimum xerror row
min_row <- which.min(cp_table$xerror)
# threshold = min xerror + its standard error
threshold <- cp_table$xerror[min_row] + cp_table$xstd[min_row]

# pick the LARGEST cp (= simplest tree) whose xerror is still within threshold
cp_1se <- cp_table$CP[max(which(cp_table$xerror <= threshold))]

cat("cp chosen by 1-SE rule:", cp_1se, "\n")
cat("cp chosen by min-xerror:", cp_table$CP[min_row], "\n")
#both suggesting 0.001, 0.0012 (earlier when penalizing, we use the xerror: tree_loss$cptable[which.min(tree_loss$cptable[, "xerror"]), "CP"], it also indicates 0.001; but then the tree is still big, so adjust it to 0.0015)
tree_rural_prune <- prune(tree_rural, cp = 0.00126)
```

```{r, fig.height=12, fig.width=20}
prp(tree_rural_prune, type=5, varlen=0, cex=0.9, extra = 2)

pred <- predict(tree_rural_prune, rural, type = "class")
confusionMatrix(pred, rural$segment_rank)
```

#### 2.2.4. Final Optimized CART Model - Urban

```{r}
urban$segment_rank <- factor(urban$segment_rank)
lv <- levels(urban$segment_rank)
K  <- length(lv)

fml <- segment_rank ~ hh.toilet.flush + med.dist + tv.yn + muslim + roof + hh.mobile +
   hh.noimp.housing + ed.sec.higher + hh.noimp.wall + marr.cohab +
  partner.working.yn + working.yn + hh.clean.fuel + med.cost + med.permis + med.alone +
  religion + rad.yn + has.mobile + floor + any.hh.dis + hh.rooms.cat +
  hh.land + hh.animal

# Loss matrix: rows = TRUE class, cols = PREDICTED class.
# w[i] = cost of misclassifying a true class-i case.
make_loss <- function(w) { L <- matrix(w, K, K); diag(L) <- 0; L }

# ---- Training-set performance for one loss setting, across all cp values ----
train_by_loss <- function(w1, w2, w3, w4) {
  w   <- c(w1, w2, w3, w4)
  set.seed(2026)
  fit <- rpart(fml, data = urban, method = "class",
               parms   = list(loss = make_loss(w)),
               control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 5))
  
  cps <- fit$cptable[, "CP"]
  
  map_dfr(seq_along(cps), function(j) {
    pruned <- prune(fit, cp = cps[j])
    pred   <- predict(pruned, newdata = urban, type = "class")
    cm     <- confusionMatrix(pred, urban$segment_rank)
    s      <- cm$byClass[, "Sensitivity"]
    sp     <- cm$byClass[, "Specificity"]
    tibble(weights      = paste(w, collapse = "/"),
           cp           = cps[j],
           n_leaves     = fit$cptable[j, "nsplit"] + 1,
           xerror       = round(fit$cptable[j, "xerror"], 3),
           !!!setNames(as.list(round(s,  3)), paste0("sens_", lv)),
           !!!setNames(as.list(round(sp, 3)), paste0("spec_", lv)),
           min_sens     = round(min(s), 3),
           mean_bal_acc = round(mean(cm$byClass[, "Balanced Accuracy"]), 3),
           accuracy     = round(unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]), 3))
  })
}

# ---- Grid of class weights ----

weight_grid <- expand_grid(
  w1 = seq(.5, 2, by = 0.25),   
  w2 = seq(0.5, 2, by = 0.25),   
  w3 = 1,
  w4 = seq(.5, 2, by = 0.25)
)
nrow(weight_grid)   

# parallel compute
plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

results <- future_pmap_dfr(
  weight_grid, train_by_loss,
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE,
                            packages = c("rpart", "caret", "dplyr", "purrr", "tibble")),
  .progress = TRUE
)
plan(sequential)


# Settings where every class is >= 80% sensitive:
# smallest tree first, then best balanced accuracy
best <- results %>%
  filter(min_sens >= 0.80) %>%
  arrange(n_leaves, desc(mean_bal_acc))
best %>% print(n = 20, width = Inf)

# ---- Refit and prune the chosen model ----
pick <- best[1, ]
w    <- as.numeric(strsplit(pick$weights, "/")[[1]])

tree_final <- rpart(fml, data = urban, method = "class",
                    parms   = list(loss = make_loss(w)),
                    control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 5))
tree_final <- prune(tree_final, cp = pick$cp)

confusionMatrix(predict(tree_final, newdata = urban, type = "class"),
                urban$segment_rank)

prp(tree_final, type = 5, varlen = 0, cex = .5)

saveRDS(tree_final, "../data/tree_urban_pruned_mk.rds")

```

#### 2.2.5. Final Optimized CART Model - Rural

```{r} 
rural$segment_rank <- factor(rural$segment_rank)
lv <- levels(rural$segment_rank)
K  <- length(lv)

fml <- segment_rank ~ hh.toilet.flush + med.dist + tv.yn + muslim + roof + hh.mobile + 
  hh.noimp.housing + ed.level + hh.noimp.wall + marr.cohab + partner.working.yn + 
  working.yn + hh.clean.fuel + med.cost + med.permis + med.alone + religion + rad.yn + 
  has.mobile + floor + any.hh.dis + hh.rooms.cat + hh.land + hh.animal

# Loss matrix: rows = TRUE class, cols = PREDICTED class.
# w[i] = cost of misclassifying a true class-i case.
make_loss <- function(w) { L <- matrix(w, K, K); diag(L) <- 0; L }

# ---- Training-set performance for one loss setting, across all cp values ----
train_by_loss <- function(w1, w2, w3, w4, w5) {
  w   <- c(w1, w2, w3, w4, w5)
  set.seed(2026)
  fit <- rpart(fml, data = rural, method = "class",
               parms   = list(loss = make_loss(w)),
               control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 5))
  
  cps <- fit$cptable[, "CP"]
  
  map_dfr(seq_along(cps), function(j) {
    pruned <- prune(fit, cp = cps[j])
    pred   <- predict(pruned, newdata = rural, type = "class")
    cm     <- confusionMatrix(pred, rural$segment_rank)
    s      <- cm$byClass[, "Sensitivity"]
    sp     <- cm$byClass[, "Specificity"]
    tibble(weights      = paste(w, collapse = "/"),
           cp           = cps[j],
           n_leaves     = fit$cptable[j, "nsplit"] + 1,
           xerror       = round(fit$cptable[j, "xerror"], 3),
           !!!setNames(as.list(round(s,  3)), paste0("sens_", lv)),
           !!!setNames(as.list(round(sp, 3)), paste0("spec_", lv)),
           min_sens     = round(min(s), 3),
           mean_bal_acc = round(mean(cm$byClass[, "Balanced Accuracy"]), 3),
           accuracy     = round(unname(cm$overall["Accuracy"]), 3))
  })
}

# ---- Grid of class weights ----

weight_grid <- expand_grid(
  w1 = seq(1, 2,   by = 0.25),    
  w2 = seq(1, 2,   by = 0.25),   
  w3 = 1,
  w4 = seq(1, 2,   by = 0.25),   
  w5 = seq(0.25, 2, by = 0.25)   
)
nrow(weight_grid)   


plan(multisession, workers = max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 1))

results <- future_pmap_dfr(
  weight_grid, train_by_loss,
  .options  = furrr_options(seed = TRUE,
                            packages = c("rpart", "caret", "dplyr", "purrr", "tibble")),
  .progress = TRUE
)
plan(sequential)


# Settings where every class is >= 779% sensitive:
# smallest tree first, then best balanced accuracy
best <- results %>%
  filter(min_sens >= 0.779) %>%
  arrange(n_leaves, desc(mean_bal_acc))
best %>% print(n = 30, width = Inf)

# ---- Refit and prune the chosen model ----
pick <- best[3, ]
w    <- as.numeric(strsplit(pick$weights, "/")[[1]])

tree_final <- rpart(fml, data = rural, method = "class",
                    parms   = list(loss = make_loss(w)),
                    control = rpart.control(cp = 0.001, xval = 5))
tree_final <- prune(tree_final, cp = pick$cp)

confusionMatrix(predict(tree_final, newdata = rural, type = "class"),
                rural$segment_rank)

prp(tree_final, type = 5, varlen = 0, cex = .5)

saveRDS(tree_final, "../data/tree_rural_pruned_mk.rds")

```

## 3. Try other methods 
### 3.1. Random Forest
#### 3.1.1. Rural National
```{r}

################################################################################
# RANDOM FOREST FOR PREDICTION SEGMENTS
################################################################################

set.seed(123)

############################ RURAL NATIONAL #############################################
predictors <- c(
  "any.hh.dis", "ed.level", "hh.mobile", "hh.animal", "hh.clean.fuel", "hh.land",
  "hh.noimp.housing", "hh.noimp.wall", "hh.rooms.cat", "hh.toilet.flush",
  "marr.cohab", "med.alone", "med.cost", "med.dist",
  "med.permis", "muslim", "religion", "occupation.cat1", "partner.working.yn", 
  "rad.yn", "tv.yn", "wealth.sum.index.cat1", "working.yn")

rf_data <- as.data.frame(rural)[, c("segment_rank", predictors), drop = FALSE]

# ---- Data prep ----
# Outcome must be a factor for classification
rf_data$segment_rank <- factor(rf_data$segment_rank)

# Character columns -> factors (randomForest won't accept character)
rf_data[] <- lapply(rf_data, function(x) if (is.character(x)) factor(x) else x)

# randomForest does NOT handle missing values the way rpart does (rpart uses surrogate splits).
rf_data <- na.roughfix(rf_data)   

# Keep the original labels so you can translate back for reporting
orig_levels <- levels(rf_data$segment_rank)

# need to change prediction labels for trainControl
levels(rf_data$segment_rank) <- make.names(orig_levels)
cls <- levels(rf_data$segment_rank)
k   <- length(cls)

# Lookup table: safe name -> original label
label_map <- setNames(orig_levels, cls)
label_map

# cross validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method          = "cv",
  number          = 5,          # 5 folds
  savePredictions = "final",
  classProbs      = TRUE
)

# try a couple of different values for mtry (num of vars picked at each node SQRT(P) is standard for categorical vars)
p <- length(predictors)
tune_grid <- expand.grid(mtry = unique(c(2, floor(sqrt(p)), floor(p / 3), floor(p / 2))))
tune_grid

##################
# Get best cut off
####################

# x/y interface keeps factors intact (the formula interface would dummy-code them)
rf_cv_rural <- train(
  x          = rf_data[, predictors],
  y          = rf_data$segment_rank,
  method     = "rf",
  trControl  = ctrl,
  tuneGrid   = tune_grid,
  ntree      = 500,
  importance = TRUE,
  nodesize = 1,
  metric     = "Kappa",   # or "Kappa", which is better if classes are imbalanced
)

probs <- as.matrix(rf_cv_rural$pred[, cls])
obs   <- rf_cv_rural$pred$obs

# Predicted segment for a given set of cutoffs
predict_cut <- function(cut) {
  factor(cls[max.col(sweep(probs, 2, cut, "/"), ties.method = "first")], levels = cls)
}

sens_by_class <- function(pred) {
  diag(prop.table(table(obs, pred), 1))     # sensitivity of each segment
}

# Multipliers per segment: < 1 = easier to predict, > 1 = harder to predict
# Segments not listed here (R4.2.NN) stay at 1
mult_grid <- expand.grid(
  R3.1.NN = seq(0.4, 1, 0.05),    # weak segment: make easier
  R4.1.NN = seq(0.4, 1, 0.05),    # weak segment: make easier
  R2.NN   = seq(0.7, 1, 0.1),     # borderline: optional small adjustment
  R3.2.NN = c(1, 1.25, 1.5, 2, 3) # perfect segment: make harder
)

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(mult_grid)), function(i) {
  cut <- rep(1 / k, k); names(cut) <- cls
  m   <- unlist(mult_grid[i, ])
  cut[names(m)] <- cut[names(m)] * m
  cut <- cut / sum(cut)
  
  pred <- predict_cut(cut)
  s    <- sens_by_class(pred)
  
  # people from other segments predicted as R3.2.NN (false positives)
  fp_R3.2 <- sum(pred == "R3.2.NN" & obs != "R3.2.NN")
  
  data.frame(
    setNames(as.list(m), paste0("m_", names(m))),   # multipliers, prefixed m_
    as.list(round(s, 3)),                           # sensitivities
    fp_R3.2   = fp_R3.2,
    min_sens  = round(min(s), 4),
    mean_sens = round(mean(s), 4),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

results <- results[order(-results$min_sens, -results$mean_sens), ]
head(results, 10)

best <- results[1, grep("^m_", names(results))]
best_cut <- rep(1 / k, k); names(best_cut) <- cls
best_cut[sub("^m_", "", names(best))] <- best_cut[sub("^m_", "", names(best))] * unlist(best)
best_cut <- best_cut / sum(best_cut)

################
# train model
################

rf_cv_rural <- train(
  x          = rf_data[, predictors],
  y          = rf_data$segment_rank,
  method     = "rf",
  trControl  = ctrl,
  tuneGrid   = tune_grid,
  ntree      = 500,
  importance = TRUE,
  nodesize = 1,
  metric     = "Kappa",   # or "Kappa", which is better if classes are imbalanced
  cutoff = best_cut
)

print(rf_cv_rural)             # CV accuracy/kappa for each mtry
plot(rf_cv_rural)
rf_cv_rural$bestTune           # selected mtry
rf_cv_rural$finalModel         # final randomForest fit on all data with best mtry

# Cross-validated confusion matrix (from the held-out fold predictions)
confusionMatrix(rf_cv_rural$pred$pred, rf_cv_rural$pred$obs)

# Variable importance
varImp(rf_cv_rural)
plot(varImp(rf_cv_rural), top = 15)

# Using the model in prediction mode for new data
rural_pred <- predict(rf_cv_rural, newdata = rf_data[, predictors])

saveRDS(rf_cv_rural, "../data/random_forest_rural_national.rds")
```

#### 3.1.2. Urban National
```{r}
predictors <- c(
  "any.hh.dis", "ed.sec.higher", "has.mobile", "hh.animal", "hh.clean.fuel", "hh.land",
  "hh.noimp.housing", "hh.noimp.wall", "hh.rooms.cat", "hh.toilet.flush",
  "marr.cohab", "med.alone", "med.cost", "med.dist", "med.permis", "muslim", 
  "occupation.cat1", "partner.working.yn", "rad.yn", "tv.yn",
  "wealth.sum.index.cat1", "working.yn")

rf_data <- as.data.frame(urban)[, c("segment_rank", predictors), drop = FALSE]

# ---- Data prep ----
# Outcome must be a factor for classification
rf_data$segment_rank <- factor(rf_data$segment_rank)

# Character columns -> factors (randomForest won't accept character)
rf_data[] <- lapply(rf_data, function(x) if (is.character(x)) factor(x) else x)

# randomForest does NOT handle missing values the way rpart does (rpart uses surrogate splits).
rf_data <- na.roughfix(rf_data)   

# Keep the original labels so you can translate back for reporting
orig_levels <- levels(rf_data$segment_rank)

# need to change prediction labels for trainControl
levels(rf_data$segment_rank) <- make.names(orig_levels)
cls <- levels(rf_data$segment_rank)
k   <- length(cls)

# Lookup table: safe name -> original label
label_map <- setNames(orig_levels, cls)
label_map


# cross validation
ctrl <- trainControl(
  method          = "cv",
  number          = 5,          # 5 folds
  savePredictions = "final",
  classProbs      = TRUE
)

# try a couple of different values for mtry (num of vars picked at each node SQRT(P) is standard for categorical vars)
p <- length(predictors)
tune_grid <- expand.grid(mtry = unique(c(2, floor(sqrt(p)), floor(p / 3), floor(p / 2))))
tune_grid


##################
# Get best cutoff 
#################

# x/y interface keeps factors intact (the formula interface would dummy-code them)
rf_cv_urban <- train(
  x          = rf_data[, predictors],
  y          = rf_data$segment_rank,
  method     = "rf",
  trControl  = ctrl,
  tuneGrid   = tune_grid,
  ntree      = 500,
  importance = TRUE,
  nodesize = 1,
  metric     = "Kappa"  # or "Kappa", which is better if classes are imbalanced

)

cls   <- levels(rf_cv_urban$pred$obs)   # U1.NN, U2.NN, U3.1.NN, U3.2.NN
k     <- length(cls)
probs <- as.matrix(rf_cv_urban$pred[, cls])
obs   <- rf_cv_urban$pred$obs

predict_cut <- function(cut) {
  factor(cls[max.col(sweep(probs, 2, cut, "/"), ties.method = "first")], levels = cls)
}

sens_by_class <- function(pred) {
  diag(prop.table(table(obs, pred), 1))     # sensitivity of each segment
}

# Multipliers per segment: < 1 = easier to predict, > 1 = harder to predict
# Segments not listed here (U1.NN) stay at 1 as the reference
mult_grid <- expand.grid(
  U2.NN   = seq(0.6, 1, 0.05),        # needs a little improvement: make easier
  U3.2.NN = seq(0.6, 1, 0.05),        # needs a little improvement: make easier
  U3.1.NN = c(0.9, 1, 1.1, 1.25, 1.5) # can give up some performance if needed
)

results <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(mult_grid)), function(i) {
  cut <- rep(1 / k, k); names(cut) <- cls
  m   <- unlist(mult_grid[i, ])
  cut[names(m)] <- cut[names(m)] * m
  cut <- cut / sum(cut)
  
  s <- sens_by_class(predict_cut(cut))
  
  data.frame(
    setNames(as.list(m), paste0("m_", names(m))),   # multipliers, prefixed m_
    as.list(round(s, 3)),                           # sensitivities
    min_sens  = round(min(s), 4),
    mean_sens = round(mean(s), 4),
    check.names = FALSE
  )
}))

results <- results[order(-results$min_sens, -results$mean_sens), ]
head(results, 10)

best <- results[1, grep("^m_", names(results))]
best_cut <- rep(1 / k, k); names(best_cut) <- cls
best_cut[sub("^m_", "", names(best))] <- best_cut[sub("^m_", "", names(best))] * unlist(best)
best_cut <- best_cut / sum(best_cut)
round(best_cut, 3)

###############
# train model
##############
rf_cv_urban <- train(
  x          = rf_data[, predictors],
  y          = rf_data$segment_rank,
  method     = "rf",
  trControl  = ctrl,
  tuneGrid   = tune_grid,
  ntree      = 500,
  importance = TRUE,
  nodesize = 1,
  metric     = "Kappa",   # or "Kappa", which is better if classes are imbalanced
  cutoff = best_cut
)

print(rf_cv_urban)             # CV accuracy/kappa for each mtry
plot(rf_cv_urban)
rf_cv_urban$bestTune           # selected mtry
rf_cv_urban$finalModel         # final randomForest fit on all data with best mtry

# Cross-validated confusion matrix (from the held-out fold predictions)
confusionMatrix(rf_cv_urban$pred$pred, rf_cv_urban$pred$obs)

# Variable importance
varImp(rf_cv_urban)
plot(varImp(rf_cv_urban), top = 15)

# Using the model in prediction mode for new data
urban_pred <- predict(rf_cv_urban, newdata = rf_data[, predictors])

saveRDS(rf_cv_urban, "../data/random_forest_urban_national.rds")

```
